ca-ab705.bill: Assessment and Placement Strategies for Community Colleges
ca-ab705.leverage_point: Parents and community members can advocate for transparency in placement practices and support for students needing additional preparation, ensuring equitable access to college-level courses.
ca-ab705.summary: Requires California community colleges to maximize the probability that students will enter and complete transfer-level coursework in English and math within one year, using high school coursework, grades, and GPA as primary placement factors[1].

ca-ab1705.bill: Community Colleges: Assessment and Placement: English and Mathematics
ca-ab1705.leverage_point: Parents and advocates can monitor local college compliance, demand data on student outcomes by demographic group, and push for targeted supports to close achievement gaps.
ca-ab1705.summary: Strengthens and clarifies implementation of AB 705 to address equity gaps, ensuring that placement systems and curricular structures at community colleges are designed for strong and equitable student outcomes[1].

ca-ab1122.leverage_point: Parents and community members can advocate for expanded dual enrollment opportunities at local high schools, ensuring equitable access and alignment with college and career readiness goals.
ca-ab1122.summary: Proposes universal access to dual enrollment programs, incentivizing College and Career Access Pathways (CCAP) partnerships and removing barriers for underrepresented students[2].

ca-sb438.bill: School Attendance: College and Career Access Pathways Partnerships
ca-sb438.leverage_point: Parents and residents can engage with school boards to demand robust CCAP programs, monitor participation rates, and ensure programs serve all student populations equitably.
ca-sb438.summary: Aims to expand and sustain CCAP partnerships between K-12 districts and community colleges, providing more students with early college credit and career pathway opportunities[2].

ca-sb305.leverage_point: Parents and community advocates can push for local colleges to provide financial aid outreach and support, ensuring students maximize available resources for college success.
ca-sb305.summary: Would require all community college students to apply for financial aid (or opt out), increasing access to state and federal grants for low-income and underrepresented students[2].

ca-sb790.bill: Postsecondary Education: State Authorization Reciprocity Agreement
ca-sb790.leverage_point: While not directly K-12, parents and community members can advocate for local districts to leverage expanded online learning opportunities for college and career readiness.
ca-sb790.summary: Authorizes California to join an interstate agreement allowing universities to offer online courses across state lines, expanding access and protecting student consumers[3].
